entities.name: Roman Crucifixion
entities.label: Movement
entities.summary: Rome reserved crucifixion for slaves, rebels, and non-citizens — it was considered too degrading for Roman citizens. Victims were nailed or tied to wooden crosses and left to die of asphyxiation, exposure, or blood loss over hours or days. Bodies were displayed on roads as deterrents. Spartacus' revolt ended with 6,000 crucifixions along the Appian Way.
